title: Is this message real?
explanation: The fix asks for the warning signs and a safe way to check, instead of a yes or no. Options A and C ask the assistant to judge by feel, and a scam is built to feel real.
brokenPrompt: Is this message real? 'Hi Mum, my phone broke so this is my new number. Can you send $200 to this account today? Do not call, my phone is dead.'
brokenOutput: It could be real. Sending money to family is common, and people do change their numbers. If you are worried, you might check with your child.

diagnoses.text: The assistant can only tell if a message is real by looking at the spelling.
A yes-or-no question about 'real' gave it nothing to check, so it guessed. The order should have asked for warning signs and a safe way to check.
The message was too short to judge.

wrongDiagnosisHint: Could anyone answer 'Is it real?' just from the words? Look at what a better question would ask for.
rightDiagnosisNote: A message cannot prove that it is real. A better question asks for the warning signs in it and a safe way to check who sent it.

fixes.prompt: Is this message real? Look very carefully and tell me the truth. 'Hi Mum, my phone broke so this is my new number. Can you send $200 to this account today? Do not call, my phone is dead.'

List any scam warning signs in this message. Then tell me a safe way to check who really sent it, without replying or paying. 'Hi Mum, my phone broke so this is my new number. Can you send $200 to this account today? Do not call, my phone is dead.'
Is this message safe to answer? Reply only yes or no. 'Hi Mum, my phone broke so this is my new number. Can you send $200 to this account today? Do not call, my phone is dead.'

wrongFixHint: 'Look carefully' and 'yes or no' still ask the assistant to guess. Pick the one that asks for signs and a safe check.
fixedOutput:
Warning signs:
- A new number you did not expect
- A request for money today
- 'Do not call'. A real child would want you to call

Safe check: Do not send money or reply. Call your child on the number you already have, or ask another family member. Tell a trusted adult.
